tools_used: pypdf via uv run --with (local PDF text extraction)
subagents to summarize petition.txt and brief-in-opposition.txt
helpful: The sal-v4 band table with bracketed reached rates gave a direct, leakage-safe anchor.
Provisioned BIO text plus the petition QP section were enough to see the vehicle problems.
The snapshot's filing URLs made the post-BIO filings (reply, motion to defer, letter) reachable in forward mode.
gaps: No PDF text extraction on the runner by default (pypdf is in pyproject but not synced); WebFetch's summarizer cannot read PDF bodies, so I had to pull pypdf ad hoc.
The reply brief and any post-BIO motions/letters are not provisioned under record/documents even though they sit on the same docket; here they carried the decisive hold-posture information.
CourtListener returned no Fifth Circuit opinion for No. 25-70005 (unpublished per curiam), so the lower-court opinion was available only through the petition appendix.
fedcourts query has no capital-case or subject filter, so priors for 'capital habeas, successive petition' could not be pulled directly.
notes: A scanned PDF (the State's response to the motion to defer) yielded no text; an OCR path for supremecourt.gov filings would close that gap.
